nodes.title: HyperCities
nodes.description: An unfinished, open field for navigating the past, present, and future of places through intersecting stories, media, and participation.

nodes.title: Thick mapping
nodes.description: A critical, layered practice of making, reading, contesting, and remaking spatial narratives.

nodes.title: Digital humanities
nodes.description: Interpretive and design-centered humanities work that uses the digital to invite multiple readings and public participation.

nodes.title: The flaneur
nodes.description: A figure of urban wandering whose movement across a city can also become movement through historical time.

nodes.title: Derive
nodes.description: Purposeful drifting: a non-linear movement through place, encounter, association, and unexpected relation.

nodes.title: Time-layers
nodes.description: Coexisting, non-simultaneous historical strata that make a present place heterogeneous.

nodes.title: Palimpsest
nodes.description: A place understood as layered traces rather than a single, clean surface or timeline.

nodes.title: Ghosts
nodes.description: Erased, muted, or absent people, structures, and histories made newly perceivable through care and narration.

nodes.title: Zoom
nodes.description: A historical method that changes the scale of attention, moving between local texture and comparative structure.

nodes.title: Counter-mapping
nodes.description: Mapping that exposes representational power and creates alternatives, tensions, and opportunities for contestation.

nodes.title: Windows
nodes.description: Situated openings in which project authors, communities, and media forms articulate different mapping practices.

nodes.title: Events
nodes.description: Unfinished, multi-scalar occurrences whose meanings emerge through witnesses, records, time, and later narration.

nodes.title: Georeferencing
nodes.description: The act of making a relation between representations; it does not discover a neutral or final ground.

nodes.title: Turtles all the way down
nodes.description: A refusal of an ultimate cartographic reference point: every base map and coordinate system is another representation.

nodes.title: Multiplicity
nodes.description: The coexistence of many voices, paths, media, scales, and interpretations without forced resolution.

nodes.title: Contingency
nodes.description: The possibility that a route, encounter, or meaning could be otherwise; a condition for straying and an open future.

nodes.title: The open future
nodes.description: Potential futures remain unclosed, inviting participation while resisting deterministic historical narratives.

nodes.title: Participation
nodes.description: The ability to contribute, annotate, witness, and contest a shared cultural record, with attention to uneven power.

nodes.title: Polyvocality
nodes.description: Multiple authors, genres, formats, and situated voices held in relation without a single neutral narrator.

nodes.title: Projection
nodes.description: A contingent technical and political choice that makes one world legible while distorting or excluding others.

nodes.title: Basemap
nodes.description: A provisional reference layer whose apparent neutrality should be questioned rather than treated as final ground.

nodes.title: Body at risk
nodes.description: Embodied proximity and vulnerability that disrupt the detached, totalizing gaze of an abstract observer.

nodes.title: Archive
nodes.description: A partial, designed record that can preserve, omit, and reconfigure traces of an event or place.

nodes.title: Singular voice
nodes.description: The irreducible witness or account that resists being fully absorbed into aggregate visualizations.
